We'd spent the whole day exploring this small island.
We completely lost track of time between the beaches, the little seafood shacks, and a hike that took way longer than the map had promised us.
By the time we checked our phones, the last ferry back to the mainland was leaving in twenty minutes.
We were still a solid thirty-minute walk from the dock.
That did not add up well at all.
We basically ran the whole way, sweaty and out of breath, dragging beach bags and a half-eaten bag of snacks.
We watched the time tick down while dodging tourists strolling along at a much more reasonable pace.
At one point I nearly dropped an entire bag of souvenirs into a fountain.
I caught it at the very last second, and honestly, it felt like the universe testing how much worse this sprint could get.
We got to the dock just in time to watch the ferry pull away from the harbor.
We were close enough to see people waving from the deck.
That honestly felt like some kind of cruel joke.
The next ferry, it turned out, wasn't until the following morning.
We were stranded on an island with absolutely no lodging booked, and we had exactly one working phone between the two of us.
We stood there for a solid minute, just staring at the empty water where the ferry had been.
We were both silently doing the math on how expensive an unplanned night on a small island was probably about to get.
We wandered around, half-panicking, until we found a tiny guesthouse with one room left.
It was run by an older couple, and they seemed genuinely amused by two exhausted tourists showing up out of nowhere at sunset.
Turns out, missing that ferry accidentally gave us the best evening of the entire trip.
We had a quiet dinner on a nearly empty patio and watched the sunset with nowhere else we needed to rush off to.
We caught the first ferry back the next morning, a little sunburned and definitely under-packed for an extra night.
But honestly, we weren't even a little mad about how the whole thing had turned out.
The older couple even packed us a small bag of pastries for the ride back.
They waved from the dock as the ferry pulled away, and somehow the whole accidental detour felt like exactly where we were supposed to end up.
Now, whenever we travel somewhere with a last ferry, train, or bus, we build in an extra hour of buffer time.
Though honestly, part of me almost misses the chaos of nearly missing it entirely.
